pages.title: 3 of 31 matters requiring a board decision are put to the board on this page, the largest carrying 4 128 of exposure, in R'000.

boardActions: Annual Financial Statements for FY2026: 10 days overdue (due 28 August 2026) — Whether to file immediately, accepting any penalty exposure.

Apr 2026: expenses for the month are a net credit — more was reversed out of expense accounts than was posted into them, so the month reports a loss even with the credit, as the period does. The quantum is that credit, 4 128; the trends panel's net profit of (1 408) is that credit plus revenue and other income of (5 536). Whether the reversals behind the credit belong to this period.

Aged debtor concentration: Blitz Fibre owes 3 192, 77.0% of all debtors owed on the aged debtors report, which come to 4 146, in R'000 — Whether to escalate, hold credit, or refer the account for write-off.
3 further matters follow on the matters page.
25 further matters are not printed in this pack; the matters page states what they come to.

notes.heading: Commentary

notes.heading: Action panel

It is machine-written and states the decision each matter is waiting on, never a recommendation.

notes.body: Revenue is turnover; Other income is what the income statement reports separately. Expenses fall in three: Cost of sales; Operating, above the operating line; Other, below it. The two income columns less the three expense columns are the month's net profit, so each row adds across.

notes.heading: EBITDA
notes.body: EBITDA for the reporting period is (1 971). The comparative period's is nil. It is operating profit plus the depreciation and amortisation charged in the period, and it is presented because a board asks for it, not because a standard requires it. Every figure above covers a month or the 12 months to Sep 2026 (part); this one covers the reporting period. The basis of preparation reconciles both to operating profit line by line.

notes.heading: What this means
notes.body: Revenue is (5 535). Turnover below zero is not a period a business can trade — it means the revenue accounts are in net debit, commonly credit notes or reversals exceeding the period's invoicing, or a receipt posted to an income account the wrong way round. Every margin in this pack divides by revenue, so each of them is reported as not meaningful rather than computed off a negative base. The pack reports the ledger as it stands; the revenue accounts should be traced before it is relied on.

footnotes.text: Figures are rounded to the nearest R'000, so components may not add exactly to the totals shown.
The prior column is the period 26 April 2025 to 31 December 2025 — 250 days, the same length as the reporting period.

The table states each line as the ledger carries it. The bridge below POSITIONS each bar by its effect on net profit — up where the line added to it, down where it took away — and COLOURS it by what the line is: green for income, red for cost, in every pack and whichever way the period ran. Operating Expenses of (3 717) in the table is labelled with that same figure on the bridge, drawn UPWARDS because that is the direction it increases profit, and in red, because it is a cost line. The label and the position are the same fact read two ways.

entries.definition: In brackets — (12 345) — for currency, percentages and ratios alike. No minus sign is used anywhere in this pack. Only a positive value takes a +.

A measure the figures cannot support. The pack prints the reason rather than a number, never a zero. A dash (–) is that zero: a figure measured and nil. A real amount too small to show at this scale prints as <1, or (<1) where it is negative.
Gross profit (revenue less cost of sales), as a percentage of revenue.
Operating profit as a percentage of revenue.
Net profit, as a percentage of revenue.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation — a non-IFRS measure: operating profit plus the period's movement on depreciation and amortisation. That movement is a NET CREDIT here — more reversed out of those accounts than posted in — so the add-back is negative and EBITDA sits below operating profit. The ledger's movement, not a sign error.
Current assets less current liabilities, in rand.
Current assets divided by current liabilities.
Cash and cash equivalents divided by current liabilities.
Total liabilities divided by total equity. Not reported on negative equity: the quotient inverts.
Operating profit divided by net interest expense. This pack captures no interest expense line, so it is reported as not meaningful.

Trade receivables over revenue, times 365 — an annualised figure on the scorecard and highlights, whatever the length of the reporting period. The trends page instead multiplies each month's ratio by the days in that month, so the two do not agree.
Trade payables over cost of sales, times 365 — annualised, whatever the length of the reporting period. Not reported where there is no cost of sales.
Debtor days plus inventory days, less creditor days — each annualised on 365 days, as above. Not reported where no account is classified as inventory.
Cash generated by operations before investing and financing activities.
Scored against the platform's default target. A metric with no target is unscored rather than assumed met; one the figures cannot support is not meaningful. Neither counts as a pass or a miss.

notes.heading: Key
notes.body: On the bridges, green is an income line, red a cost line and dark ink a total; the two also differ in lightness, so a monochrome copy still separates them. The balance sheet's bands are one ink at three lightnesses, legended on the chart. Red on the scorecard marks a missed target.
